description: The fastest, litest AI Gateway. Rust core with Python SDK. Call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format with cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, and logging [Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, VertexAI, vLLM, Nvidia NIM]
vibe: Write code that reads like prose, test only what you own, and never let AI slop into the repo.
highlights: Comments are treated as tech debt and banned unless they explain complex business logic, serve as tool input, or mark a TODO/FIXME with a reason.
Tests must fail when the feature breaks, not just when code structure changes; mutation testing should show >90% kill rate.
Never pin external facts (vendor prices, third-party fields, dates) as literals; assert invariants your code guarantees instead.
Human-facing text must avoid emojis, em dashes, semicolons, colons, bulleted lists, and AI-sounding patterns like 'It's not X, it's Y'.
Lint and type suppressions must name the exact rule and include a reason; `# type: ignore` is banned.
assessment: This file enforces a rare discipline: it treats comments as DRY violations, demands mutation-tested regression tests, and bans external fact pinning, which together prevent the slow rot of AI-generated code. The tone is uncompromising but practical, offering concrete alternatives (Pydantic validation over Any, immutable comprehensions over mutation) rather than vague platitudes. It is a masterclass in setting boundaries that keep a large codebase maintainable without sacrificing velocity.
